members.name: Dr. Junjia Liu
members.bio: PhD in Robotics, CUHK. Deep expertise in embodied intelligence and robot manipulation — humanoids, bimanual coordination, dexterous hands, imitation & reinforcement learning. Creator of the ORGA architecture.

members.name: Dr. Yitao Yang
members.bio: PhD in large models & AI infra, CUHK. Former researcher at Microsoft Research Asia. Led large-scale Agentic automated ops systems in ByteDance Infra.

members.name: Dr. Shengting Cao
members.bio: JD, CUHK. 5+ years in capital markets, 80+ financing deals, and deep involvement managing funds exceeding USD 1B.

about.metaDesc: Xianova Robotics focuses on zero-shot generalization for robot manipulation with the object-centric ORGA architecture.
about.label: About
about.title: About Xianova
about.company: Xianova Robotics focuses on zero-shot generalization for robot manipulation. We propose the object-centric ORGA architecture so robots understand object structure, spatial constraints, and interaction from few demonstrations — instead of memorizing motion trajectories — and extrapolate across novel objects, scenes, and embodiments.

technology.metaDesc: ORGA — object-centric representation for generalization: object-centric features → geometric constraint extraction → zero-shot transfer.
technology.heroDesc: Object-centric extraction of transferable geometric constraints and spatial structure for zero-shot manipulation

principles.title: Object-centric representation
principles.desc: Anchor manipulation understanding in object geometry and interaction — not absolute trajectories in camera space

principles.title: Geometric constraint extraction
principles.desc: Distill latent spatial constraints and structural priors from few demonstrations into reusable manipulation knowledge

principles.title: Zero-shot transfer
principles.desc: Generalize to novel objects, scenes, and embodiments without per-instance retraining

technology.demoDesc: From human-centric multimodal capture to cross-scene expansion and cross-embodiment retargeting — how one skill understanding transfers to new environments and robot platforms

demos.title: Human-centric multimodal teaching
demos.desc: Wearable sensing records vision, touch, and motion during manipulation — high-quality demos for generalization models

demos.title: One demo, a thousand scene variants
demos.desc: Object-centric representation expands a single demonstration across new poses, layouts, and lighting — no re-collection

demos.title: Tabletop skills on a bimanual humanoid
demos.desc: Pick-and-place on a Paxini humanoid shows the same skill transferring zero-shot across robot bodies

demos.title: Map human motion onto a humanoid
demos.desc: SparkUMR retargets everyday actions like drinking onto Fourier GR3 while preserving contact and posture

demos.title: Desktop organization, retargeted
demos.desc: Human motions for arranging a phone and laptop transfer to GR3 — fine manipulation that travels with the skill

demos.title: One kitchen skill, many robots
demos.desc: The same mixing and scooping routine drives different humanoid platforms — a unified skill model across embodiments
